key_insight: Post-training alignment methods can make small language models stronger than a proprietary baseline for biomedical data-to-text generation, especially for medication leaflet-style outputs.
clinical_relevance: This work suggests aligned small models may help generate clearer patient-facing medication information from structured biomedical data.
method: Compared Qwen-based small language models with SFT, DPO, ORPO, and GRPO.
Used a medicine package leaflets dataset and additional openFDA drug label data for cross-dataset testing.
Evaluated outputs with ROUGE and semantic similarity metrics.
evidence_signal: The abstract reports that aligned SLMs outperformed GPT-5 overall, ORPO beat SFT baselines, and GRPO was the most robust across datasets.
watch_item: Results are based on specific datasets and metrics, so real-world usefulness may vary when the model is deployed on new drug texts or patient communication settings.
paper_title: Exploring Post-Training Alignment of Small Language Models for Biomedical Data-to-Text Generation: A Case Study of Medication Leaflet
